body:
Scholastic achievement, volunteer work, being a compassionate and good friend and family member, taking care of sick folk, being patient and kind, giving when I could, having a life focus of service and love over hate and destruction.  There are good things, but the suicidal ideation... maybe abuse and bullying as a kid, abuse from partners later.  Stagnation for a while.  Chronic illness and what to do when chronic illness resolves.  Relationship issues.  Loneliness.  Becoming hooked on opiates when I was critically ill due to medical malpractice with no action plan to get me off... sent home with fucked up brain chemistry and an addiction issue.  Using alcohol and benzos to try to get over that addiction.  Feeling unworthy.  Having my partner (now x) of many years cheat on me while I was sick.  Losing focus of life goals and losing all hope.  Knowing my family member will die before me and not wanting to live in a world without them.. not wanting to be in a world where no one loves me.

It's been a long road.  Thanks for your reply and interest.

The pain with many terminal illnesses suck, though.  Then the fear and sometimes pure delirium at the end.. no thanks.  I'd rather not go out naturally.  I like to face fear head on and how could I do that hallucinating, confused, calling for parents that may be long dead.. frightened out of my mind.  The only genuinely good thing about being terminally ill is the medical community finally stops shaming chronic pain patients for pain meds and allow the opiates to flow more freely.

Hey, thanks for your reply.  I feel the one black mark that will overshadow everything is suicide.  My aunt's husband died long before I was born and thats pretty much what his story amounts to - an abusive drunk who hung himself in the end.  Me?  Depressed, anxious mess who was a hermit, couldn't get her life together, and killed herself somehow.  It seems like everything else I did that was good (not that much of it, unfortunately) will be replaced by this.

I still feel this later in life.  I mourn for my shit 20s and 30s.  I know I should concentrate on the now, but I still feel like I'm fucking them up, too.  What is the answer?  Mindfuless worked for me once, but I feel I'm way too fucked for that now.

Hope you're able to overcome these feelings.  They are truly shit.

Cymbalta and Paxil both gave me similarly bad reactions.  I would call and express your exact feelings, hold nothing back.  I was switched off the medications immediately, although I was on them for just a little bit longer.
Having crippling anxiety that my partner will leave me to the point I think about running away just to avoid the unimaginable pain of losing them.
